# MATLAB compiled-adapter foundation and campaign ledger

Campaign: #502–#507, followed by the gated #501 release/benchmark campaign. Implementation branch: `feat/matlab-compiled-adapters`, based on qualified v4 main `806ed7ef141c2f8baef451134f9b90f1f390c540`. The independent `bench/three-model-release` branch at `751db305` is preserved. No release tag or public support claim is made by this foundation.

## Ownership and execution contract

MATLAB owns scientific state, modal construction, integration, forcing/callback order, custom operations, and output. Native objects own prepared numerical execution. `WVOwnedStratifiedModalSource` owns authoritative MATLAB modal arrays and shares its preparation implementation with `WVStratifiedModalRecord`; production construction performs no NetCDF round trip and solves no eigenproblem. The native runner and MATLAB adapter share `WVNativeVariablePolicy`. On the qualified Apple Silicon native path this chooses FFTW, Accelerate, compact spectra, prepared workers, and the existing tiled advection pipeline.

The MATLAB adapter stores a native handle and the originating transform's runtime-only `compiledSourceIdentity`. This opaque MATLAB handle token has transient backing storage, so MATLAB MAT-file restoration receives a fresh owner too. It rejects foreign models, including same-shape models with different stratification. It is neither a state generation nor a persisted property. The initial MEX call borrows coefficient arrays only until that invocation returns; C++ evaluation scopes close before outputs publish. Errors unwind owning C++ objects before invoking MATLAB error dispatch. Native handles are monotonic, isolated from legacy handles, locked while live, and released by deletion or module cleanup.

`transformCreate`, `transformPrepare`, `transformEvaluate`, `transformMetadata`, and `transformDelete` define the initial private ABI. One replaceable prepared request bounds plan retention. The proof supports Hydrostatic `u`, `v`, `w`, `eta` and optional nonlinear flux. A mixed flux/field call owns a forcing-engine scope and reads its cached physical bundle. A field-only call owns a field-service scope. It never nests two owners of the same kernel. Metrics include both evaluation owners and actual kernel validation/phase counters. These call-scoped proofs do not yet provide a general MATLAB RHS/diagnostic event spanning several MEX invocations.

For #506, explicit MATLAB event scopes must follow mutation of Ap, Am, A0, t, t0, retries, restore, and dense output. Never infer identity from same time or buffer addresses. A retained cross-call evaluation requires native-owned immutable state or a documented MATLAB ownership mechanism and explicit generation. Preserve custom callback ordering and MATLAB variable-cache invalidation; do not replace custom operations based only on output names. MATLAB scientific behavior remains backward compatible.

## Operation matrix and implementation map

| Numerical operation | Constant H / NH | Hydrostatic | Boussinesq | Stratified QG | Barotropic QG |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| State-to-field, components, first derivatives | Existing native kernel; migrate legacy adapter | Native kernel; four-field private proof | Native kernel | Native A0 field kernel | Native A0 field kernel |
| Physical-to-state projection | Existing UVEta / UVWEta methods | UVEta | Separate UVEta and UVWEta | UVEta-to-A0 and QGPV-to-A0 | QGPV-to-A0 |
| Raw F/G synthesis and projection | Existing numerical providers; expose correct primitive shapes | Existing prepared vertical and horizontal operators | Distinct balanced and grouped wave operators | Existing prepared operators | Identity vertical operations plus Fourier provider |
| Full-grid differentiation / integration | Existing FFT calculus | Existing F/G calculus | Existing F/G calculus | Existing QG calculus | Horizontal calculus |
| Nonlinear advection and forcing | Existing native engines | Private optimized proof | Existing native engine | Existing native engine | Existing native engine |
| Registered fields, reductions, density diagnostics | Existing field service | Existing field service | Existing field service | Existing field service | Existing field service |
| Custom operations, arbitrary forcing callbacks, sampling orchestration | MATLAB owns callback behavior in all families; supported numerical calls dispatch compiled |

Important shape distinction: MATLAB `transformFromSpatialDomainWithFg/Gg/Fio` consumes a Fourier/vertical array, not a real physical volume. Boussinesq `transformToSpatialDomainWithFg/Gg/Fw/Gw` returns `[Nz,Nkl]` Fourier/vertical arrays. The native kernel's `transformToSpatial/transformFromSpatial` includes the horizontal FFT, so those methods cannot directly implement the raw MATLAB primitives. Expose existing prepared numerical operations without inserting a redundant forward/inverse FFT pair. Preserve explicit `K2unique`/`iK2unique`, P/Q preconditioning, and QGPV normalization. Freeze the precise primitive ABI before dispatching family implementation agents.

The public `computationalBackend="matlab"|"compiled"` selection will remain runtime-only. MATLAB stays the default. A claimed compiled primitive must run natively or raise an actionable unsupported error. Arbitrary MATLAB callbacks remain MATLAB code; adding a forcing must not disable the compiled backend. The #504 wave and #505 QG adapters precede #506 consumer integration and #507 qualification. The final #501 table requires all three interfaces for all three models, with setup excluded.

## Build identity and qualification remaining

The legacy capability record validates the installed provider identity but does not bind all current numerical source files to the MEX binary. Complete source-set fingerprints/build receipts and clean installed-package qualification before advertising the expanded adapter. Source-selection metadata records foundation file identities without rewriting historical qualification receipts. Module metrics now account for both legacy and new handles and report the actual MEX lock. Bridge-version metadata rejects an older installed binary with a rebuild instruction. Preserve existing tags and the standalone runtime.

Direct and MEX worker counts differ (direct uses two pointwise workers; MEX uses the shared host policy); this is numerical comparison, not a timing comparison.

MATLAB caches are invalidated outside each reference timer. Host idleness was not established; these are feasibility observations only. Maximum finite relative error `1.97e-15`.

Native source 599,274 bytes; kernel including source 281,630,004 bytes; forcing engine including kernel 423,635,911 bytes; additional field service 89,279,266 bytes; field plan 1,200 bytes. Combined reported scientific execution lower bound 512,916,377 bytes excludes host/catalog and opaque provider overhead. Native coefficient input copies are zero; caller result arrays are required output transfers. Plans and retained storage stay stable, phase/state validation increase once per call, duplicate producers remain zero, live evaluation storage is zero after return.

- `docs:check` passed with zero route failures and zero generated-tree differences. Targeted production analyzer passed; its inventory tests pass with additive expectations for the three new MATLAB files. No whole native or MATLAB suite was repeated.

## Frozen next primitive boundary

Use the existing `WVStratifiedModalOperator` enum for three thin public methods on H/B/SQG kernels: `applyVertical(operation, WVComplexConstView, WVComplexView)`, `applyVerticalColumn(operation, retainedColumn, inputColumn, outputColumn)`, and the retained `horizontalForward`/`horizontalInverse` pair. Full complex shapes are `[Nj,Nkl]` for modes and `[Nz,Nkl]` for Fourier/vertical grids; single-column views have second dimension one. All operations use existing prepared operators and scratch, with no second modal source, matrix preparation, or FFT plan. Compact split staging uses existing private scratch; interleaved paths use caller views directly. Preserve the active-call and protected-state output rules. Unsupported operations and shapes fail explicitly.

H and SQG accept reconstructF/projectF/reconstructG/projectG. B additionally exposes its prepared wave and cross-family operations. Fio uses exact zero-wavenumber membership; B uses the wave F projection for that column. These raw operations contain no Fourier transform. Retained Fourier entry points execute exactly one existing horizontal transform.

Generalize the existing full-grid horizontal derivative service to a positive integer order while keeping the first-order overload. Use one FFT pair and a correctly normalized `(ik)^n` multiplier. Even-order Nyquist contributions must be retained; composing first derivatives would incorrectly discard them. This is an explicit compatibility requirement for MATLAB n=2/4, verified on full-grid frequencies outside the retained WV subset.

At the MEX boundary, add `transformOperation(handle, operationName, inputsCell, optionsStruct) -> resultStruct`. Result values remain in ordered cells with native metrics. Use strings for operation/family/component choices, and strict per-operation input shapes. State-dependent operations take explicit immutable state/generation through the evaluation interface; arbitrary coefficient matrices passed to raw basis operations must never be interpreted as a physical-state field. The coordinator owns dispatch and lifecycle; family agents own bounded kernel wrappers and parity tests against this boundary.

Final review corrections: both native registries now share one MEX exit callback. Source-owner identity uses a hidden sealed handle token, not a resettable persistent counter. MAT-file restoration, `clear functions`, and legacy/new handle coexistence in both creation orders pass focused regressions. The analyzer inventory passes at 181 files. These lifecycle-only corrections leave the measured numerical path and storage capacities unchanged; the measured and final MEX hashes are distinguished in the qualification receipt.
